reader_notes: Gap 2 is the one that takes a moment: 'Naturally' wins on discourse logic (introducing the received view before the rebuttal), while 'Conversely' is tempting on a shallow read but does not introduce a converse of the preceding claim.
Gap 3 tests polarity ('far from decisive' vs 'far from ineffective') cleanly; gap 4's accede/concede/precede/recede set is a fair morphological family with only 'concede' taking a that-clause.
Passage is idiomatic, well-paced journalistic English; the 11-second vs 22-second detail lands the argument nicely.
